entries.title: Leviticus 10:1
segments:
Censer; a fire-pan for sacred uses. 
 
  Strange fire; common fire--not that which was kindled by the Lord on the altar.

This event seems to have taken place in the sanctuary, whither they had gone in an irreverent and presumptuous manner to burn incense. 
 
Recklessness in divine worship, and the offering of our own excited and proud emotions instead of that humble and obedient spirit which he requires, are peculiarly offensive to God.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:2
segments:
From the Lord; from his visible glory on the mercy-seat. 
 
  Devoured; killed. 
 
Great sins and great trials may speedily follow the reception of great mercies.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:3
segments:
Them that come nigh me; especially those who conduct religious worship. 
 
  Held his peace; submitted without a murmur to the righteous judgment of God. 
 
Prompt and cheerful submission to God, and hearty acquiescence in his will, under trials, however great, is a fruit of the Spirit which peculiarly honors him, and is useful to men.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:5
segments: Out of the camp; for burial.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:6
segments: Uncover not--neither rend; avoid all appearance of mourning.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:7
segments:
Not go out; not suspend any of the duties of the ministry, but continue to discharge them. 
 
Regard for our friends, or sorrow on account of their death, must not lead us improperly to manifest grief, or to neglect our appropriate duties.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:9
segments: Do not drink wine nor strong drink; it is supposed that Nadab and Abihu had been drinking, and became excited; that this was one cause of their transgression; and that God enjoined on his ministers, when about to engage in public worship, entire abstinence from the use of intoxicating drink, that they might not be unfitted for their work.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:10
segments: Holy and unholy--unclean and clean; things which God forbids in his worship, and those which he requires.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:11
segments: The use of wine or strong drink is exceedingly dangerous, and should be abstained from, especially by ministers when about to engage in sacred public dities; that they may rightly conduct the worship of God, and make known his will to the people.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:14
segments: A cheerful reception of the good things of Providence, and at proper times and in suitable circumstances even feasting with our families on the fruits of divine kindness, is not only allowable, but is a duty, the right performance of which will promote the divine glory and our own highest good.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:18
segments: Ye should--have eaten it; if its blood had been brought into that part of the tabernacle called the sanctuary, or holy place, they were to burn it without the camp; if not, they were to eat it.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:19
segments:
Such things; the death of his two sons. 
 
  If I had eaten; joined with his family in feasting, while thus heavily afflicted. 
 
  Should it have been accepted? would it, under those peculiar circumstances, have been suitable or pleasing to God? 
 
Some things which on ordinary occasions would be right, proper, and useful, may without sin be omitted on occasions of great affliction and distress; and some things which on ordinary occasions would not be proper, may at such times be done.

entries.title: Leviticus 10:20
segments: He was content; satisfied that God would not be displeased with Aaron and his sons for what they had done.
